title: Crash-Safe Memory
summary: Persist agent progress and effect receipts so a replacement worker can resume safely after an abrupt process or machine failure.
overview: Crash-safe memory preserves the workflow facts needed for correct recovery after volatile process state disappears. It includes accepted inputs, state revisions, pending commands, tool receipts, and completion markers. Saving conversation text alone cannot establish whether an external operation happened before a crash.

The critical design question is the commit boundary. Durable state must precede acknowledgment, and external effects need idempotency or reconciliation when they cannot share a transaction with workflow storage. Write-ahead logging protects a database transaction under its configured durability assumptions; it does not automatically make the surrounding distributed workflow exactly once.

production.poc: A prototype should survive a forced process kill between two tool calls without losing the accepted task.
production.production: Production persists revisions and effect identifiers, coordinates queue acknowledgment with durable commits, and tests duplicate delivery.
production.scale: Enterprise scale defines recovery point and recovery time objectives, replication behavior, backup restoration, and schema compatibility for old unfinished workflows.

components.name: Durable state database
components.role: Stores workflow revisions and committed task progress.

components.name: Command outbox
components.role: Records intended external work in the same transaction as its originating state change.

components.name: Receipt ledger
components.role: Associates tool results with stable operation identifiers.

components.name: Recovery worker
components.role: Acquires a lease and reconstructs pending work after failure.

components.name: Snapshot archive
components.role: Provides recoverable history beyond a single running database instance.

flow.title: Accept durably
flow.description: Commit the task identifier and initial state before acknowledging receipt to the caller.

flow.title: Record intent
flow.description: Write the next state and tool command together using a transaction or equivalent atomic boundary.

flow.title: Execute command
flow.description: Deliver the command with a stable idempotency key and retain its external receipt.

flow.title: Commit outcome
flow.description: Persist validated results and mark the command complete before advancing the workflow.

flow.title: Recover ownership
flow.description: A replacement worker acquires a fenced lease and reads the last committed revision.

flow.title: Resolve uncertainty
flow.description: Reconcile incomplete commands against external receipts before deciding whether execution may repeat.

diagrams.title: Durable intent and recovery
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant W as Agent worker
 participant D as Durable database
 participant T as Tool service
 participant R as Recovery worker
 W->>D: Commit state and command intent
 W->>T: Execute with operation key
 T-->>W: Receipt
 W->>D: Commit receipt and progress
 R->>D: Read pending commands after crash
 R->>T: Reconcile operation key
 T-->>R: Existing outcome
diagrams.caption: A crash between the tool result and database commit is resolved by operation identity, not blind replay.

diagrams.title: Ambiguous effect recovery
diagrams.code:
stateDiagram-v2
 [*] --> IntentCommitted
 IntentCommitted --> EffectSubmitted
 EffectSubmitted --> ReceiptCommitted: Result persisted
 EffectSubmitted --> OutcomeUnknown: Worker crashes
 OutcomeUnknown --> Reconciling: Recovery lease acquired
 Reconciling --> ReceiptCommitted: Existing effect found
 Reconciling --> IntentCommitted: Safe retry established
 Reconciling --> HumanReview: External outcome unresolved
 ReceiptCommitted --> [*]
diagrams.caption: Unknown is a durable recovery state and must not be silently converted to failed.

useCase.title: Surviving a crash during account-maintenance review
useCase.situation: An internal agent verifies supporting documents and submits approved account-maintenance requests.
useCase.problem: A worker can crash after submission but before recording the response.
useCase.requirement: Recover the review without submitting the maintenance request twice.
useCase.architecture: The workflow database stores command intent, a stable case key, and the maintenance-system receipt.
runtime: The replacement worker finds a pending submission for the case.
It queries the maintenance system by the original key and records the existing receipt.
useCase.failure: If the external system cannot identify the submission, the case pauses for reconciliation instead of assuming failure.
useCase.impact: Measure recovered task completeness, duplicate-effect incidents, and reconciliation age; memory durability is useful only when business effects remain coherent.

tradeoffs.cost: Adds write latency to each boundary.
Increases replay distance and possible unacknowledged work.
Requires explicit consistency and failover assumptions.

failures.detection: An accepted task disappears after restart.
failures.recovery: Persist acceptance before acknowledging and replay durable ingress records.

failures.detection: Two workers attempt the same revision.
failures.recovery: Reject stale fencing tokens and reconcile any external effects.

mistakes.fix: Store workflow state, tool intent, and effect receipts.
Design idempotency and reconciliation across the external boundary.
Inject kills at every commit boundary and inspect recovered invariants.

whenToUse: Use for long-running or high-value workflows.
Use with at-least-once queues and replaceable workers.
Use when accepted work must survive machine loss.
whenNotToUse: Avoid durable orchestration for disposable stateless inference.
Do not promise zero data loss without storage guarantees.
Avoid automatic replay of ambiguous non-idempotent commands.
checklist: Test crashes between effect and receipt commit.
Document replication and backup recovery objectives.
Exercise restoration of unfinished workflow schemas.
